rules.sentence: The presence of crystals cannot exclude septic arthritis with certainty.
Septic arthritis can occur concurrently with gout or pseudogout in less than 5% of cases.
Meanwhile, a low synovial fluid glucose level suggests joint infection.
Still, low glucose levels are present in only about 50% of patients with septic joints.
Rheumatoid arthritis may also have low synovial fluid glucose.
A cell count with WBCs of more than 50,000 cells/mm3 is considered diagnostic for septic arthritis.
However, lower counts do not rule out a joint infection.
A prosthetic joint with WBCs greater than 1,100 cells/μL is considered septic.
Glucose will be less than 50% of the serum level.
In rheumatoid arthritis, expect decreased viscosity and poor mucin clot formation.
